summary.text: Amanda Dow is the Liberal candidate for Yan Yean at the 2026 Victorian election. She is a primary school teacher with an education degree who earlier worked in sales and administration, and her party page says she teaches at one of the largest schools in the electorate and lives in Doreen. Her campaign focuses on crime, the cost of living, local schools and road upgrades such as fully duplicating Donnybrook Road.

priorities.text: Road upgrades, including full duplication of Donnybrook Road

sources.title: Yan Yean: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Amanda Dow, Liberal for Yan Yean, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Andrew Bell is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Yan Yean at the 2026 Victorian election. On his party page he describes himself as a Mernda local who works in the public sector, belongs to the Community and Public Sector Union and organises in the community. He lists campaigns on racism, war, the treatment of asylum seekers, climate change and Palestine, and recent work to rebuild the CPSU.

priorities.text: I will continue to fight for a fairer society
Tackling inequality and the housing crisis
Resisting far-right politics that blames migrants and multiculturalism
Solidarity with the people of Palestine

sources.title: Yan Yean: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Gufran Mohammed is the Greens candidate for Yan Yean at the 2026 Victorian election. He moved from India to Melbourne in 2017, and his past jobs include audit and management roles at the firms Deloitte and KPMG and running the business side of a school. The ABC's guide says he went on to found a not-for-profit finance firm that advises schools; on his party page he says he left the school job after arguing for spending on support for students with disability.

occupation.text: Founder of a not-for-profit finance firm advising schools

priorities.text: represent people, not corporations, and achieve better futures for us all
Making sure schools can identify students with disability so they get funded support

sources.title: Yan Yean: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Gufran Mohammed, Candidate for Yan Yean, Australian Greens

summary.text: Jeremy Johnson is One Nation's candidate for Yan Yean at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide describes him as working in cybersecurity and as a former army reservist. He stood for One Nation in the federal seat of McEwen in 2025, polling about 6.6 per cent of the primary vote. His One Nation candidate page refused automated requests, so we could not read it.

sources.title: Yan Yean: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Electoral results for the Division of McEwen, Wikipedia

summary.text: Lauren Kathage has been the Labor member for Yan Yean since the 2022 election, succeeding the retiring MP Danielle Green. Before Parliament she worked in community development in Australia and overseas, from housing and homelessness projects to running national programs, and she has been an acting speaker since 2024. She is recontesting Yan Yean in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Manager of national programs training health workers and supporting regional communities and children with disability
prior_roles.note: Both sources say she did this before her election; neither gives a start year.

prior_roles.role: Community worker leading housing and homelessness projects
prior_roles.note: Neither source gives the years; Wikipedia says 15 years of community work, Parliament more than twenty years of volunteering and work.

priorities.text: Development that puts the community at its centre
Local jobs and good transport so families can build a good life
Every opportunity for people with disability

summary.text: Sinan Okatan is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Yan Yean at the 2026 Victorian election. He grew up in Melbourne's north, studied construction management and engineering, and has a background in waste and recycling policy; he now manages greenhouse climate and fertigation control projects in horticulture. His party page says he and his family have lived in the district for about five years, and that his campaign centres on cost-of-living relief, housing and animal welfare.

occupation.text: Project manager in the horticulture sector

priorities.text: Local infrastructure that does not harm animals or the green wedge
Working with local farmers on a shift to more sustainable agriculture

sources.title: Yan Yean: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Sinan Okatan for Yan Yean, Animal Justice Party Victoria

summary.text: Troy Cheers is the Libertarian candidate for Yan Yean at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide gives only personal interests (he follows Richmond and plays paintball), and neither the party's Victorian candidate page nor any other source we could use had published a biography or policy statement for him as at early November 2026.

sources.title: Yan Yean: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
